done_when: close runs the release-checkout sync test (or forge sync --check) when a change touches the workflow generator or the templates and fails with one line naming the file to regenerate; and when the pinned release is newer than the newest published tag in Forge's own repo, close runs Forge from the source checkout instead of failing; new and existing repos get it on upgrade

known.title: Close crashes for sample-data prototypes with an existing workflow
Not done: close does not consistently use the source checkout for an unpublished pin
Close skips a missing generated client workflow

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a sample-data prototype closes a fix while retaining its existing workflow.
In sample-data mode, `prcheck.ships()` returns an empty dictionary (`src/forge/prcheck.py:234`), but this lookup indexes it whenever the committed workflow exists. Close therefore raises `KeyError` before review. Retaining an existing workflow in this mode is an established path in `tests/test_sample_setup.py:85-106`.
findings.title: Close crashes for sample-data prototypes with an existing workflow

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 3, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - close a source fix from the main checkout after its worktree has merged an unpublished release bump.
The Done-when requires: "close runs the release-checkout sync test (or forge sync --check) when a change touches the workflow generator or the templates and fails with one line naming the file to regenerate; and when the pinned release is newer than the newest published tag in Forge's own repo, close runs Forge from the source checkout instead of failing; new and existing repos get it on upgrade". `check_pin` checks the caller's checkout and returns when its older pin matches the installed version (`repo.py:937-941`). Close then reads the fix worktree's already-new pin as its previous pin (`close.py:87,247`), so no handoff occurs and the old Forge continues. Two other paths still fail: generated-guide conflict repair fetches the unpublished tag directly with `--with` (`close.py:775-780`), and `_older` ignores prerelease suffixes, so a published `v1.3.0-rc.1` prevents fallback for an unpublished `v1.3.0` (`repo.py:1003,1057-1061`).
findings.title: Not done: close does not consistently use the source checkout for an unpublished pin

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - an earlier-adopted sample-data client without a Forge workflow turns sample data off and enables checks.
When the workflow is absent from HEAD, `committed` is `None` and this condition skips the comparison, although normal-mode sync would generate the file (`src/forge/prcheck.py:466`). Close can proceed without the promised regeneration message; CI-configured repos then lack the workflow that produces the expected checks. The earlier-adopted fixture has no workflow, and sync deliberately leaves workflows alone in sample-data mode.
findings.title: Close skips a missing generated client workflow

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a source pull request changes the workflow generator or a template.
This proof invokes `forge test --pytest` directly and substitutes a receipt-writing function for the release sync test. The separate release test invokes sync but does not close a source change. Both can pass if close or its CI path skips the selected test, allowing a stale generated workflow through. The promised behavior needs coverage through close with the real sync check.
findings.title: Gate: tests/test_close_requires_current_workflow.py::test_2_source_generator_changes_run_the_release_sync_test

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a source fix is being closed as an unpublished release bump arrives.
The proof closes `missing-fix` and expects the immediate not-started refusal, so it never exercises an actual close, an in-flight pin change, or generated-file conflict repair. It passes while the direct `--with` fetch in `src/forge/close.py:775-780` still fails for the unpublished release. A real item must reach close's completion path to prove this behavior.
findings.title: Gate: tests/test_forge_source_uses_unpublished_pin.py::test_3_close_runs_an_unpublished_forge_source_pin_from_its_checkout

stop.reason: Owner chose one more round: fix the five review findings

why: A change to the workflow generator (prcheck.py or the templates) can merge without the regenerated .github/workflows/forge.yml, which turns main red (it happened on 18 Nov 2026), and after a release bump merges, a branch that merges main pins a release that is not published yet, so close fails with 'Failed to resolve --with requirement' until the release is out
